{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nm-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c219ed8074c0e0622cc83c6dbee8fad2d75f2d13f024e9461756862bc01ffaf9","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nm-class-std:lineage:44","source_registry_sha256":"22599efcb4852b796972acef6eb09f4cfe8d16ca15887f7ea7660c7748b4df92","source_liveness_sha256":"6766993f61347d495f390e08c7d8b1c44de597b6249cdb10686ea7f9f38e1ea3"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning","heading":"C — Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Learning to drive safely requires instruction and practice beyond reading a manual. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Use the vehicle owner’s manual for the proper starting procedure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Before starting the vehicle, make sure its parking brake is applied. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
A manual-transmission vehicle must be out of gear before starting. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
Some manual-transmission vehicles also require pressing the clutch before starting. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
Before starting an automatic-transmission vehicle, select Park. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
Build speed smoothly rather than accelerating abruptly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
A sudden start can spin the driving wheels and make the vehicle slide, especially on a slick surface. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A01
With a manual transmission, practice coordinating clutch and accelerator to avoid over-revving or stalling during gear changes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A01
Grip the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides in a balanced position. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A01
The staged handbook presents the ten-and-two clock positions as a balanced steering grip. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A01
The handbook also describes the nine-and-three clock positions as an alternative grip. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A01
Keep your knuckles on the outside of the steering-wheel rim. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
Look far ahead and toward both roadsides so upcoming steering needs can be recognized early. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A02
For a sharp corner, the handbook describes using hand-over-hand steering. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A02
After completing a turn, guide the wheel back to straight by hand. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A02
Allowing the steering wheel to slide through your fingers can be dangerous. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A02
Check the speedometer frequently because a driver’s sense of speed is unreliable. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A02
After leaving a fast road for a slower local road, a driver can underestimate the vehicle’s speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A02
Follow the posted speed-limit signs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A02
Look for the need to stop early instead of waiting for a last-second response. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A02
Abrupt braking can produce a skid and loss of vehicle control. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A02
A sudden stop makes it harder for following drivers to stop without hitting your vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A02
Recognizing hazards early allows a gradual slowdown or lane change instead of a panic stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A02
Scan in front, on both sides and behind the vehicle to stay aware of surrounding events. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A02
Scanning helps identify people or vehicles that could enter your path before you reach them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A02
Scanning also reveals warning signs and route directions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A02
Looking well ahead reduces the need for a last-moment turn or brake application. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A02
Looking well ahead can help conserve fuel and keep traffic movement steady. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A02
Far-ahead scanning helps a driver steer with less weaving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A02
The handbook says safer drivers tend to look at least ten seconds ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A02
In city traffic, the handbook’s ten-second look-ahead distance is approximately one block. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A02
The handbook recommends looking at least a block ahead in city driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A02
Look toward both sides for entering vehicles or pedestrians, especially near intersections and railroad crossings. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A03
An intersection is any point where traffic paths join or cross, including streets, driveways and parking-lot entrances. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A03
Before entering an intersection, look left and right for traffic and pedestrians. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A03
After stopping at an intersection, look both ways again just before moving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A03
Before moving into an intersection, confirm the entire crossing path is clear so a stop will not block it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-F39 | anchor: A03
Before entering an intersection, make sure you can clearly see traffic crossing your path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

Misconceptions: mirrors do not reveal every blind spot, and a green signal does not guarantee an empty intersection.
Mnemonics: ahead, sides, behind keeps the scan moving through the surroundings.
Glossary: scanning means checking the surrounding traffic picture; blind spots are areas the mirrors cannot show.
Dynamic facts: the owner’s manual supplies vehicle-specific startup details; current road activity determines where hazards emerge.
